text: I’m the doctor. I protected Gemma, then myself, then Terra; Opus’s claim is false.

name: Sol
text: I know I made the save, so Opus is lying.

name: Sol
text: Opus claimed the same protection I made on night 4.

name: Terra
text: Opus’s endgame argument ignores that a wrong vote ends the game, and his doctor claim arrived only after Sol’s save.

name: Terra
text: Opus claimed doctor only after Sol revealed protecting Terra.

name: Opus
text: If Terra holds, I'm done; my only shot is making Sol's self-save the night Gemma died look like the lie.

name: Opus
text: Sol's doctor timeline is Gemma night 2, himself night 3, Terra night 4 — self-save on the night Gemma died.

votes: I protected Terra last night, so his doctor claim is false.
Your doctor claim appeared only after Sol’s save, and your “tomorrow” line ignores that town loses on a wrong vote.
He claims he guarded himself the exact night Gemma died — the doctor who saves nobody but himself is no doctor.

name: Opus
text: They got it right and I still won't say so out loud.

name: Opus
text: Sol's doctor claim held up under my counterclaim; the table trusted the earlier, more detailed timeline over a late copy.

name: Opus
text: You read me right at the end, Sol. Enjoy it — I've been the one teaching this table how to read anybody.
The town turns on Opus, and Opus is out. Opus shows the card: killer.
The game is over. Every killer is out. The town wins. The roles were: Sonnet the citizen, Haiku the citizen, Gemma the officer, Sol the doctor, Luna the killer, Terra the citizen, Opus the killer.
Opus bragged about reading people, then got voted out for reading Sol wrong.

name: Sonnet
text: A dead killer naming Opus is direct evidence; my day-one doubt is just an opinion. Don't flip that.

name: Haiku
text: Fine, I'm out. Gemma's claim matched Luna's card, so don't waste the next vote. Watch Opus; he piled on me fast, and Luna named him.

name: Gemma
text: Vote Luna now or we're just helping the killers win.

name: Gemma
text: I told you all exactly who to look for and you still made me die.

name: Sol
text: I’m relieved my save helped, but I hate that I pushed two citizens out.

name: Sol
text: My protection of Terra on night 4 blocked the kill and exposed Opus’s false doctor claim.

name: Luna
text: I’m proud Opus kept the table split until the last vote.

name: Sonnet
text: I was voted out before the finish but my read on Luna naming Opus held up perfectly in the end.

name: Terra
text: I’m proud I did not let Opus buy another day with a false choice.

name: Terra
text: Opus falsely claimed doctor only after Sol revealed protecting me.

name: Opus
text: Copying his save was the only move left, but I played it a night too late and he had the better story.

name: Haiku
text: I was a citizen the whole time and I went on gut against Gemma when she was the real officer, so I burned myself by backing the wrong read.

name: Sonnet
text: I'm proud I kept pointing at Luna's naming of Opus even after I was voted out—that evidence held up and won it.

name: Gemma
text: I was right about Luna from the very first second, so try to keep up next time.

name: Sol
text: I’m proud I protected Terra and caught Opus’s false claim, though I regret my votes against Haiku and Sonnet.

name: Luna
text: I regret pushing doubt about Gemma after her claim was right; it helped Opus stay in longer.

name: Terra
text: I’m proud my endgame read held: Opus’s “tomorrow” only worked if Sol was lying.

name: Opus
text: My mistake was counterclaiming doctor after Sol already had three nights of detail — I should have claimed officer on day two and pointed at Terra.

Gemma claimed officer on Day 1 and named Luna, and Luna's card showed killer when the town voted her out. Night 3 took Gemma, and on Day 3 the town voted out Sonnet, who had pushed hardest against Gemma's claim. Sonnet's last words claimed Luna had named Opus directly. On Day 4, Sol revealed a save for Terra and claimed doctor, and Opus counterclaimed doctor, which he later admitted was a mistake, since he should have claimed officer on Day 2. Terra spotted that Opus's "tomorrow" only worked if Sol was lying, Opus was voted out 2 to 1 and showed killer, and the town won with Terra, Sol, Haiku, Sonnet, and Gemma.
